title: Staying in New York and sending for his family
summary: After Maine he stayed in New York, sent for his wife and child, and worked as an upholsterer by day.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Oh, yeah, afterwards. Because I went up -- you know, after we went through that stunt -- after Maine, you know. And the band came back through there, you know, we stopped in New York, and I just stayed in New York.
Oh. Oh.
See, I didn't go back -- I didn't go back --
You didn't go back, but you sent for her?
No. I sent for her. I sent for her and my kid.
Oh, I see.
So, there was method in your madness?
Yeah. I had to --
That's how you got out?
Yes.
So, and before you sent for her you'd probably got yourself the job at the Yeah Man? Am I right?

Yes. Yes. I'd gotten my job at the Yeah Man -- I'd been working --- doing other things, you know what I mean. Like I worked as an upholsterer, making chairs and what-not. Then after she got there I had two jobs. I'd work at the upholstery and at night I'd work at the Yeah Man. I'd work at the upholstery during the daytime, and at the Yeah Man at night. You know, I had two jobs I worked.
What year would you think we're up to with the Yeah Man? I wonder how old you'd be then?
Oh. It's around thirty-something.
For the Yeah Man?
Yeah. Thirties.
Yeah. That's what he said -- nineteen -- or twenty perhaps?
Yes. Right. Right.
Because you were nineteen when you went back, and you stayed till you were twenty.
Twenty. That's right.
